articles.title: Paths in pieces
articles.summary: Linux distributions and package managers audit just-built binaries for non-relocatable absolute paths. If a binary contains a path /path/from/build/machine, it might not run on the end-user's machine. A basic grep on the binary or a slightly more sophisticated $ strings bin/app | grep /path/from/build/machine using GNU binutils's strings will detect these paths, but the answer is no, at least when using GCC and targeting x86-64, because string constants end up literally in the binary, not just detected by string constants. This is due to GCC's optimization of std::string{PREFIX}, which splits the string into overlapping pieces of 16 bytes and stores them in xmm registers, effectively filtering out the relevant bits from g++ -O2 -S -masm=intel.
